items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-16
items.q: And I'd show you Jim Europe who was a colored man playing. And they both have the same rhythm.

ctx.x: You don't see anything in front of me that I take notes from, only just from what comes to my mind. That's why I don't have it in chronological order. I can only tell you what I can think of at the time. Maybe my talk may be gobbled up a little bit, that I might put this one before the other one, the other one before the other one. But I am telling you the true facts of this music. It was in Chicago where I changed the rhythm. They had a certain dance team. They were doing a castle walk. And up in the north,…
Can you hold it a second?

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-06-14
items.q: There were a few recordings by coloured bands. There was Jim Europe on Victor... But one's only got to listen to those and compare them with the original Dixieland Jazz Band to realise that the one is Ragtime and the other is Jazz.

ctx.x: Today is Sunday, June 14th, 1959. This is Brian Rust of London, England. I'm sitting in the living room of Nick LaRocca's home, 2218 Constance Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. Mr LaRocca has done me the honour of making a tape recording of his voice telling his story of how he came to create jazz and his opinions and the whole story of the growth of the music. And he's asked me to give my side of it, how I came to be interested in the music and what it means to me and to English people now. Until 1936, I'd never…

it's easy enough to listen to them. I've only got to listen to those and compare them with the original Dixieland Jazz Band to realise that the one is Ragtime and the other is Jazz. The original Dixieland Jazz Band isn't called Jazz for Nothing. There are other musicians having laid claim to having made the first jazz records. I have just compiled a book which lays great stress on the dates of recordings. The first jazz recordings in the book, not Ragtime, the first jazz recordings, are those by the original…
